tier_reason: The shootout itself would meet A (public harness miloyip/nativejson-benchmark src/tests/sheredomjsonhtest.cpp, clang 7.0, build/premake5.lua optimize "Full" with -march=native, Core i7-4980HQ), but the measured 2016-era json.h failed 9 of 34 parse-validation and 7 of 9 string tests in the same suite's sample/conformance.csv (accepted raw tab and newline inside strings, trailing content and malformed exponents; string03-string09 fail, consistent with no \u escape decoding), and those hot-path correctness gaps were fixed later (current json.h decodes \u escapes; raw control characters rejected in commit 5db3857 on 2026-10-02), so the later-fixed-bug rule caps it at C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Parse time in ms, json.h vs nlohmann v2.0.3: canada.json 9.418 vs 55.591 (5.9x), citm_catalog.json 5.077 vs 9.875 (1.9x), twitter.json 2.351 vs 7.010 (3.0x); three-file total 16.846 vs 72.476 ms (4.3x) (ratios derived from page data). Also parses faster than JsonCpp (142.458 / 14.587 / 8.477 ms), Jansson (78.465 / 22.656 / 10.935 ms) and cJSON (15.574 / 5.580 / 3.517 ms). Stringify json.h vs nlohmann: canada.json 29.355 vs 76.315 ms (2.6x), citm_catalog.json 4.034 vs 7.178 ms (1.8x), twitter.json 0.978 vs 4.239 ms (4.3x) (ratios derived from page data). RapidJSON is still faster than json.h (4.755 / 1.950 / 1.227 ms parse).
corrections.workload: Parse of canada.json, citm_catalog.json and twitter.json from an in-memory buffer into a DOM, time in ms. Because json.h keeps numbers as text, the harness (src/tests/sheredomjsonhtest.cpp) walks the tree after json_parse and calls atof() on every number with the result discarded; stringify times json_write_minified plus an emulation walk that sprintf's into a discarded local buffer.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang 7.0 64-bit (README: 'MacBook Pro (Retina, 15-inch, Mid 2015, Corei7-4980HQ@2.80GHz) with clang 7.0 64-bit', also in the result file name); build/premake5.lua release configuration uses optimize "Full" plus buildoptions -march=native
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-4980HQ @ 2.80GHz, MacBook Pro (Retina, 15-inch, Mid 2015), macOS 64-bit (README and result file name)
corrections.caveats: Numbers are the independent nativejson-benchmark sample run (README 'Update on: 2016-9-9') on a 2014-era CPU with clang 7.0, a 2016-era json.h and nlohmann v2.0.3; nlohmann/json has been reworked since. The measured json.h did less work than the baselines: in the same suite's sample/conformance.csv it failed 9/34 parse-validation tests (pass01 rejected; fail02, fail07, fail08, fail10, fail25 raw tab, fail27 raw newline, fail29, fail30 accepted) and 7/9 string tests (string03-string09, consistent with not decoding \u escapes), while nlohmann passed all validation and string tests. Current json.h decodes \u escapes and gained fixes in 2026 (reject numbers with no digits after a sign, 2026-10-01; reject raw control characters in quoted strings, 2026-10-02; comment after a number, 2026-10-06), so the measured parser was more permissive and today's ratios may differ. json.h does not convert numbers to doubles; the harness's emulation calls atof() and discards the result, which the compiler may drop, so number conversion cost (large on canada.json) may not have been paid at all; the stringify emulation memcpy's the number payload pointer as a double and formats it into a discarded buffer, and json.h's writer copies number text verbatim with no double-to-string work. The json.h README makes no speed claim and links no benchmark; the win is a derived comparison between rows of a third-party shootout (the suite author also wrote RapidJSON, which beats json.h). Public-domain dedication (Unlicense), no patent grant.

notes: Numbers match the CSV rows exactly (Scheredom json.h (C) and Nlohmann (C++11) rows), so the evidence is real and the entry stays; downgraded A to C under the later-fixed-correctness rule because the shootout's own conformance results show the measured json.h skipped validation and \u decoding work that it now performs, and the number post-pass discards atof results. Shortcomings to record: measured 2016 build failed 16 conformance tests (raw control characters, trailing content, malformed exponents, \u escapes) later fixed; numbers kept as strings so parse and stringify skip float conversion; harness atof result discarded; stale 2016 run against nlohmann v2.0.3. Metadata confirmed: Unlicense, 841 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-10-06 (main).

tier_reason: First-party single-run Google Benchmark output in PARSING.md from public code (benchmark/configurable.cc, -O3 -DNDEBUG in benchmark/CMakeLists.txt), but compiler, compiler version, nlohmann version and the exact CPU model are not stated, so it falls short of A and is not independent.

corrections.workload: Google Benchmark run (benchmark/configurable.cc) over the repo's benchmark/input.json (newline-separated JSON packets): parse each packet to a DOM (Dart from_json, which in this build tokenizes with sajson and then lowers into Dart's sorted finalized buffer or dynamic heap), key lookups on pre-parsed results, and serialize back to a string.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 -DNDEBUG plus dart_default_compile_options (benchmark/CMakeLists.txt); the benchmark CMake defines DART_USE_SAJSON when sajson.h is found, which switches Dart's parser to sajson; compiler and version not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from a single run on a 2018 laptop (the doc itself calls single-run output noisy and says the graphs use 16 repetitions, which are images not text). nlohmann version (found as a system install by find_path) and compiler are not stated, so tier A is not met. Dart is not a tokenizer of its own here: the table was regenerated in commit 3d45bc0 ('Added a new, stupid-fast, sajson based parser', 2019-06-01), where Dart's from_json parses with sajson (include/dart/connector/json.tcc under DART_USE_SAJSON) and then lowers into the Dart buffer; that commit replaced the RapidJSON-backed finalized-parse figure of 66174 ns with 27682 ns. A default library build without the use_sajson option parses through RapidJSON and is slower than the quoted figure, so the 9.2x win over nlohmann mostly reflects sajson versus nlohmann; sajson alone parses in 14360 ns and the project's text says sajson is the choice for raw parse speed. The 'within about 50% of RapidJSON' sentence predates the sajson path. The key-lookup row measures lookups in Dart's sorted flat buffer on pre-parsed packets, not parse work. Dart requires lexicographically sorted object keys. The repo's LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 although the list tag said MIT. The repo was archived by the owner on Jul 16, 2024 and the last commit is 2021-09-11.
